activities.name: Cold-Water Surf Clinic on Cox Bay Beach
activities.description: You will gear up in a thick 5mm hooded wetsuit to brave the crisp Pacific swells under the guidance of a local pro instructor. This clinic covers ocean safety, pop-up mechanics on the sand, and reading the rugged breaks of Canada's surf capital. Paddling out into the mist-shrouded, pine-fringed water to catch your first real green wave is an unforgettably exhilarating experience.
activities.duration_note: Available year-round, but winter brings heavy expert swells; beginners should target May to September. Price includes board and full winter-grade wetsuit package.

activities.name: Blackcomb Mountain Backcountry Heli-Skiing
activities.description: You will board a high-performance helicopter to escape the crowded resort lines and ascend to untouched, wide-open powder bowls deep in the Coast Mountains. Guided by an avalanche safety expert, you will carve fresh tracks down pristine glaciers and steep glades. The absolute stillness of the wilderness combined with miles of untracked snow delivers the ultimate winter adrenaline rush.
activities.duration_note: Strictly seasonal from December to April. Requires strong intermediate to advanced skiing/snowboarding ability and includes mandatory avalanche safety gear and training.

activities.name: Richmond Night Market Culinary Safari
activities.description: You will dive straight into the neon-lit, high-energy maze of North America’s largest Asian night market to sample cutting-edge street food trends. Follow your nose to specific, highly rated stands to crunch into classic Taiwanese night-market style fried chicken, slurp freshly torched abalone, and cool off with towering mango shaved ice. It is a sensory overload of sights, smells, and chaotic culinary creativity that perfectly defines the West Coast's modern food culture.
activities.duration_note: Seasonal operational limits apply; open weekends only from late April through mid-October. Cash is highly recommended as many vendor stalls do not accept cards.

activities.name: Zodiac Whale Watching Tour in the Salish Sea
activities.description: You will don a full-body bright orange exposure safety suit and climb into a high-speed, rigid-hulled inflatable Zodiac boat designed to skim rapidly across the water. Your marine biologist guide will pilot you into deep coastal channels to safely observe resident and transient orca pods, massive humpback whales, and barking sea lions. Bouncing over the ocean waves with the wind in your face while listening to whale hydrophone calls creates an intense connection to the coastal wilderness.
activities.duration_note: Peak whale activity runs from May through October. The open-air Zodiac ride can be bumpy and physically demanding; not recommended for individuals with chronic back issues.

activities.name: Craft Cocktail Tasting in Historic Gastown
activities.description: You will wind your way through the historic cobblestone corridors of Gastown to experience Vancouver's premium cocktail culture at boundary-pushing institutions like The Keefer Bar and Guilt & Co. Sip artisanal spirits mixed with house-made botanicals and locally foraged ingredients while listening to intimate, live underground jazz acts. It is a sophisticated way to discover how the city's historical roots blend seamlessly into its chic, contemporary urban nightlife.
activities.duration_note: Advance weekend table reservations are critical for these specific venues. Note that in British Columbia, spirits cannot be bought at standard convenience stores; they are restricted to BC Liquor Stores or private vendors.

activities.name: Stanley Park Seawall Guided Biking Architecture Tour
activities.description: You will hop on a premium multi-speed hybrid bicycle to cruise along the famous 9-kilometer paved loop that hugs the ocean shoreline of Stanley Park. Stop along the route to admire towering, authentic First Nations totem poles at Brockton Point and gaze at the sprawling downtown Vancouver skyline across the harbor. The effortlessly flat path offers continuous, stunning vistas of the Pacific Ocean on one side and ancient, deep-green Douglas fir forests on the other.
activities.duration_note: Highly recommended from May to October for optimal weather, though bike rentals operate year-round. Participants must be comfortable riding in dedicated bike lanes alongside pedestrian traffic.

activities.name: Scandinave Spa Thermal Baths Experience
activities.description: You will submerge yourself in an expansive, text-free, silent outdoor oasis hidden completely within a dense canopy of old-growth spruce trees. Follow the age-old hydrotherapy cycle by heating up in a wood-burning Finnish sauna, plunging into a crisp, ice-cold mountain water pool, and resting by an open-air outdoor fireplace. It provides a profoundly peaceful, meditative escape to deeply relax your muscles after a long day of rugged alpine exploration.
activities.duration_note: A strict digital detox policy is enforced with no phones allowed on site. Advanced online booking is strongly recommended for peak ski weekends to avoid long entrance waitlists.

activities.name: Spirit Bear Wilderness Expedition
activities.description: You will journey into the ancestral territory of the Kitasoo/Xai'xais Nation, traveling deep into isolated, misty coastal fjords by boat and on foot to track the elusive Spirit Bear. Guided by Indigenous cultural experts, you will sit quietly along rushing salmon streams waiting for a glimpse of this rare, cream-white black bear variant. Immersing yourself in the silent, moss-draped ancient ecosystem offers a rare, spiritually grounding wilderness experience found nowhere else on earth.
activities.duration_note: Strictly seasonal from August through October during the annual salmon run. Requires multi-month advance booking due to extreme luxury eco-lodge capacity caps and strict conservation permits.

activities.name: Plain of Six Glaciers Backcountry Trek
activities.description: You will lace up your hiking boots to journey past the brilliant turquoise waters of Lake Louise, ascending a steady alpine trail wrapped in monumental mountain scenery. Sweat your way up through old-growth forests to a historic, rustic Swiss-built stone teahouse operating entirely without electricity or running water to enjoy a fresh scone. Continuing past the teahouse leads you directly to a jaw-dropping lateral moraine viewpoint overlooking the massive, cracking crags of Victoria Glacier.
activities.duration_note: Requires a valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass ($11-$25 CAD daily) and seasonal parking fees ($42 CAD at Lake Louise shores). Best completed from late June through September when trails are snow-free.

activities.name: Athabasca Glacier Ice Explorer Tour & Skywalk
activities.description: You will climb aboard a massive, custom-engineered Ice Explorer all-terrain vehicle sporting massive six-foot tires to drive directly onto the ancient Columbia Icefield. Step out onto the thick glacial ice to feel the sheer chill of the glacier and fill a personal water bottle with pure, freezing-cold meltwater. Afterward, you will step out over the edge of a cliff onto a glass-bottomed architectural walkway suspended 280 meters above the roaring Sunwapta Valley below.
activities.location: Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre, Highway 93, AB
activities.duration_note: Operational season is strictly restricted from early May to mid-October. Requires a Parks Canada vehicle entry pass. Dress in thick winter layers as wind speeds on the glacial surface are extreme.

activities.name: Alberta Prime Steak Tasting at Caesars Steak House
activities.description: You will settle into a plush leather booth at a legendary Calgary institution that has been perfecting local beef preparation since 1972. Watch master chefs thick-cut aged, grain-fed Alberta beef to order before searing it over an open flame broiler to lock in rich, buttery juices. Paired with a classic Caesar cocktail—which was famously invented right here in Calgary—it offers the definitive taste of authentic Western Canadian ranching heritage.
activities.location: Caesars Steak House, 512 4 Ave SW, Calgary, AB
activities.duration_note: Advance dinner reservations are mandatory. The restaurant enforces a smart-casual dress code. Perfect year-round experience unbothered by seasonal weather changes.

activities.name: Sulphur Mountain Sunset Gondola Ride
activities.description: You will soar high above the pines in an enclosed glass cabin, ascending 698 vertical meters to the bustling summit peak of Sulphur Mountain. Walk out along the extensive wooden mountaintop boardwalk to Sanson's Peak to watch the golden hour light paint six raw mountain ranges in brilliant shades of pink and orange. End the evening on the open-air rooftop terrace, warming your hands around a blazing fire pit while looking over the glowing town lights down in the valley.
activities.location: Banff Gondola Base Station, Mountain Ave, Banff, AB
activities.duration_note: Dynamic pricing applies based on real-time seasonal demand; booking far in advance online secures the lowest rates. The Sunset Festival with live outdoor musical acts runs nightly from June to September.

activities.name: Glacial Lake Wilderness Cruise
activities.description: You will step aboard a custom-designed, heated lake cruise boat to explore the deep, wind-swept waters of Banff’s largest glacial lake. Your captain will guide you deep into a rugged mountain trench while interpretive guides share fascinating Stoney Nakoda First Nations histories and geological legends. Reaching the remote Devil's Gap reveals an incredible view where the sheer vertical rock walls of the Rockies meet the flat edge of the Alberta plains.
activities.location: Lake Minnewanka Boat Docks, Banff, AB
activities.duration_note: Operating window runs from mid-May to mid-October. Parking at the lake docks is tightly regulated by Parks Canada and fills early; taking the local Roam Transit Route 6 bus is highly encouraged.

activities.name: Calgary Stampede Evening Show & Rodeo Tickets
activities.description: You will take your seat in a packed, high-energy stadium to witness the world's premier professional outdoor rodeo tournament and chuckwagon races. Watch elite cowboys wrestle steers and tame bucking broncos before the track transforms into a massive musical stage production ending with a spectacular fireworks display. It is an unbridled, immersive celebration of historic cowboy culture and community spirit that takes over the entire city.
activities.location: Stampede Park, 1410 Olympic Way SE, Calgary, AB
activities.duration_note: Strictly limited to a 10-day window in early July each year. Tickets sell out months in advance; book early to secure central grandstand views. Accommodation prices in Calgary double during this week.

activities.name: Alpine Craft Beer Crawl at Banff Ave Brewing
activities.description: You will step off the chilly mountain streets into a bustling two-story brewpub to sample crisp beers brewed on-site using pure, mineral-rich glacier water. Grab a seat at the bar to try the iconic, award-winning Beaver Tail Pale Ale alongside a diverse crowd of international travelers and local ski instructors. It is a warm, unpretentious local hangout that captures the true essence of classic Rocky Mountain après-ski culture.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Note that Alberta regulations dictate liquor can only be purchased from specialized retail liquor stores, meaning you cannot find alcohol in local grocery or convenience shops.

activities.name: Kananaskis Nordic Spa Hydrotherapy Circuit
activities.description: You will don a complimentary robe to explore a modern 50,000-square-foot outdoor wellness complex beautifully nestled against a backdrop of sheer mountain peaks. Move systematically through hot alpine pools, invigorating cold plunges, and aromatic eucalyptus steam rooms designed to stimulate circulation and ease stress. It is a serene, adult-only outdoor playground where you can completely reset your body and mind surrounded by quiet alpine forests.
activities.duration_note: Operates beautifully across all seasons—sitting in the outdoor pools during a winter snowfall is highly rated. Guests must be 18 years or older; bookings open exactly 4 weeks in advance online.

activities.name: Niagara City Cruises Voyage to the Falls
activities.description: You will throw on a protective recyclable poncho and board a state-of-the-art catamaran to sail directly into the roaring basin of the Canadian Horseshoe Falls. Feel the tremendous, thundering vibrations of 600,000 gallons of water plunging over the edge every single second right in front of you. Navigating into the blinding, thick white mist and feeling the sheer physical spray of the falls is an intense, bucket-list sensory experience.
activities.location: 5920 Niagara River Parkway, Niagara Falls, ON
activities.duration_note: Full boat operations are seasonal from April through November depending on river ice conditions. Prepare to get completely wet despite the provided plastic poncho; protect all non-waterproof electronic items.

activities.name: CN Tower EdgeWalk Extreme High-Wire Experience
activities.description: You will strap into a heavy-duty safety harness and step out onto a 1.5-meter-wide metal ledge circling the outside tip of the tower's main pod. Suspended 356 meters above the pavement with no railings or windows, you will be guided by professionals to lean out backward directly over the city streets. Looking straight down between your feet at the microscopic cars below delivers an unmatched, heart-pounding adrenaline rush.
activities.location: CN Tower, 290 Bremner Blvd, Toronto, ON
activities.duration_note: Operates daily from May through October, weather permitting (canceled in high winds or electrical storms). Stringent breathalyzer and security screening protocols are enforced prior to stepping outside.

activities.name: St. Lawrence Market Peameal Bacon Sandwich Crawl
activities.description: You will weave through the historic, brick-walled aisles of a world-famous market to join the bustling queue outside Carousel Bakery. Order the iconic Toronto staple: a warm, soft kaiser roll packed with thick, juicy slabs of grilled cornmeal-crusted peameal bacon. Drizzle it with sweet honey mustard, grab a hot coffee, and eat it on the outdoor steps while watching locals buy fresh artisanal produce inside the century-old market hall.
activities.location: St. Lawrence Market, 93 Front St E, Toronto, ON
activities.duration_note: St. Lawrence Market is strictly closed on Mondays. The bakery counter accepts card payments, but cash will help you move through the fast-paced morning queues much quicker.

activities.name: Rideau Canal Skateway Winter Expedition
activities.description: You will lace up your ice skates to glide along the frozen surface of a UNESCO World Heritage site, which transforms into the world's largest natural skating rink every winter. Wind your way past Canada’s stunning, gothic Parliament Buildings while crisp winter air fills your lungs. Stop at a wooden trailside hut directly on the ice to reward yourself with a warm, pastry BeaverTails treat coated in brown sugar and fresh lemon juice.
activities.duration_note: Strictly weather-dependent, typically opening from January to early March. Access to the canal ice is entirely free; the stated price covers a full skate and safety helmet rental from local downtown booths.

activities.name: Live Indie Music Tour of the Legendary Horseshoe Tavern
activities.description: You will step past the historic checkerboard floors of an iconic live music venue that has served as the launchpad for legendary bands like The Tragically Hip and Blue Rodeo since 1947. Grab a cold local craft pint at the front bar before moving into the back room to watch emerging indie rock acts tear up the historic stage. The gritty, high-energy atmosphere offers a genuine look into the foundational roots of Toronto's underground music scene.
activities.location: Horseshoe Tavern, 370 Queen St W, Toronto, ON
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Ticket prices fluctuate depending on the performing band. In Ontario, retail alcohol sales are handled via the LCBO and select grocery outlets—not at standard corner stores.

activities.name: Canadian War Museum Architectural & Heritage Tour
activities.description: You will explore a world-renowned architectural landmark, moving through thought-provoking galleries that house a massive collection of historic tanks, military aircraft, and deeply moving personal artifacts. Stand inside the somber, concrete Memorial Hall to witness the sun illuminate the tombstone of Canada's Unknown Soldier precisely at 11:00 AM on November 11th. The museum's raw design features sustainable grass roofs and textured walls that vividly tell a powerful story of human conflict and national identity.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Highly recommended to book tickets online in advance to skip morning entry queues. General admission is completely free for everyone on Thursday evenings from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM.

activities.name: Multi-Day Backcountry Canoe & Wildlife Circuit
activities.description: You will paddle a lightweight Kevlar canoe across a network of pristine glass-like lakes, portaging your gear across wilderness trails to camp at remote, isolated backcountry clearings. Wake up early to catch the morning mist rising off the water while watching wild moose graze along boggy shores and listening to the echoes of common loons. It is a classic Canadian wilderness experience that completely detaches you from urban life.
activities.duration_note: Best from June through September. Requires booking backcountry camping permits months ahead via Ontario Parks. Price covers high-quality multi-day canoe rental, safety paddles, PFDs, and basic camping permits.

activities.name: Old Québec Historic Cobblestone Walking Tour
activities.description: You will step straight into the past as you walk through the only fortified city walls remaining north of Mexico, exploring cobblestone lanes dating back to 1608. Follow your expert local historian through the historic Lower Town to gaze up at the towering, fairy-tale brick architecture of the iconic Fairmont Le Château Frontenac. Running your hands along stone ramparts while listening to stories of historic military sieges makes you feel like you've crossed the Atlantic into Europe.
activities.duration_note: Operates year-round. The walking path features steep inclines and stone staircases; comfortable walking shoes are required. Winter tours offer a magical snow-covered landscape but require heavy thermal wear.

activities.name: Authentic Poutine Pilgrimage at La Banquise
activities.description: You will slide into a brightly colored booth at a legendary 24-hour eatery that has been celebrating Québec's national dish since 1968. Order a piping-hot, classic 'La Reguliere'—a massive mound of hand-cut golden fries topped with squeaky fresh cheese curds and smothered in a rich, velvety brown gravy. Watching the cheese slowly melt under the hot gravy while eating alongside a lively local crowd delivers the definitive, unpretentious flavor of Montréal.
activities.location: La Banquise, 994 Rue Rachel E, Montréal, QC
activities.duration_note: Open 24 hours a day, year-round. Expect long lines extending out the front door during late-night weekend shifts or beautiful summer afternoons. Vegetarian gravy options are readily available.

activities.name: St. Lawrence Estuary Kayaking with Beluga Whales
activities.description: You will glide a sea kayak through the deep waters where the Saguenay River meets the St. Lawrence Marine Park, paddling beneath massive rock cliffs. Float quietly in the water to watch pods of small, ghostly-white beluga whales surface near your boat alongside minke and blue whales. Hearing the sharp breaths of these white whales breaking the silent surface of the water creates a magical encounter with one of Canada's most protected marine species.
activities.duration_note: Seasonal window runs strictly from June through September. Strict park conservation regulations require kayakers to maintain a mandatory 400-meter viewing buffer from endangered beluga whales.

activities.name: Jazz Night Out at the Historic Upstairs Jazz Bar
activities.description: You will head down a flight of stone steps into an intimate, brick-walled basement lounge widely ranked among the world's premier jazz clubs. Settle in close to the stage to watch exceptional local trios and international jazz icons perform live, complex sets. The dark, candle-lit room paired with incredible acoustics provides a classic bohemian nightlife experience that showcases Montréal's historic love affair with jazz.
activities.location: Upstairs Jazz Bar & Grill, 1254 Mackay St, Montréal, QC
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Shows require purchasing a specific cover ticket alongside advanced table bookings. In Québec, beers and wines can be bought in corner stores (dépanneurs), but spirits are exclusive to the SAQ.

activities.name: Aura Immersive Light Show at Notre-Dame Basilica
activities.description: You will step inside an architectural masterpiece from 1829 to experience a multi-sensory light and sound show created by the world-famous Moment Factory. Watch the soaring neo-Gothic vaulted ceilings, ornate hand-carved wood structures, and deep blue altarpieces illuminate in stunning orchestral sync. The multimedia performance masterfully highlights the building's intricate art, design, and history, transforming the historic space into a modern canvas.
activities.location: Notre-Dame Basilica, 110 Notre-Dame St W, Montréal, QC
activities.duration_note: Runs year-round on selected evenings. Tickets must be purchased online in advance as weekend shows regularly sell out completely. The experience is fully indoors and wheelchair accessible.

activities.name: Laurentian Mountains Via Ferrata Cliffside Climb
activities.description: You will clip your safety harness onto a heavy steel cable to traverse a steep, sheer rock face high above the rolling Laurentian forests. Scale vertical rock walls using anchored iron rungs, steady footbridges, and narrow zip lines under the guidance of a professional mountain climber. Reaching the panoramic summit peak offers sweeping views of the deep blue Lake Tremblant nestled among rolling hills.
activities.location: Mont-Tremblant National Park, National Trailhead, QC
activities.duration_note: Operates from mid-May through October. Requires standard physical fitness and zero fear of extreme heights. Price includes all specialized climbing gear and park entry fees.

activities.name: Traditional Maple Sugaring Feast at Sucrerie de la Montagne
activities.description: You will travel deep into an old-growth maple forest to experience a designated heritage site that harvests sweet maple sap using traditional methods. Tour the wood-fired boiling shacks before sitting down at long wooden tables for a massive, family-style Québécois feast featuring maple-glazed ham, meat pies (tourtière), and crispy pork ears. Finish the experience outside by rolling hot, gooey maple taffy directly onto fresh white snow using a wooden stick.
activities.duration_note: The peak traditional 'sugar shack' season runs strictly from late February through April during the sap run. Booking reservations months ahead is critical for weekend dining spots.

activities.name: Nordik Spa-Nature Thermal Hydroptherapy Experience
activities.description: You will explore North America's largest outdoor spa complex, beautifully built into the natural rocky landscapes right on the edge of Gatineau Park. Float weightlessly in the stunning Källa saltwater pool—a large underground pool filled with 12 tons of therapeutic Epsom salts. Alternating between intense panoramic saunas and crisp cold waterfalls hidden in the forest offers a deeply refreshing escape that restores your body's natural balance.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round across all weather conditions. Guests must be 16 years or older. Bathrobes and towels are available on-site; booking weekend admission online in advance is highly recommended.

activities.name: Hopewell Rocks Ocean Floor Walking Tour
activities.description: You will hike down a flight of stairs to walk along the muddy ocean floor beneath massive, multi-story sea stacks known as 'Flowerpot Rocks.' Explore hidden sea caves carved by the planet's highest tides, which rise up to 16 vertical meters every single day. Just six hours later, you will watch the exact area you walked on fill with water, transforming the massive stone towers into small rocky islands surrounded by kayakers.
activities.duration_note: Park operations run from mid-May to mid-October. Check the daily tide charts carefully prior to visiting; access to the rocky ocean floor is strictly prohibited during high tide cycles for guest safety.

activities.name: Peggy's Point Lighthouse Sightseeing Excursion
activities.description: You will walk across vast, wave-swept granite rocks to view one of the world's most famous and photographed coastal lighthouses. Gaze out at the crashing Atlantic surf while sea spray fills the air, then explore the historic, active fishing village nearby to see colorful wooden boats bobbing in the harbor. Standing on the granite coast watching the deep blue waves crash against the rocks offers a classic, timeless maritime experience.
activities.location: Peggy's Point Rd, Peggy's Cove, NS
activities.duration_note: Open year-round with completely free public access. Strict safety warning: stay far back from the dark, wet granite rocks close to the water, as unpredictable rogue waves can pull visitors into the sea.

activities.name: Traditional Nova Scotian Lobster Dinner at The Grand Banker
activities.description: You will take a seat at a waterfront restaurant in a UNESCO World Heritage town to crack open a fresh Atlantic lobster harvested directly from local waters. Dip the sweet meat into rich, warm garlic butter alongside a hot bowl of traditional, creamy maritime seafood chowder packed with fresh haddock and scallops. Looking out at the harbor while enjoying your fresh catch provides an authentic culinary experience tied to generations of seafaring history.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round, but fresh lobster availability peaks from May to July during the prime local harvesting seasons. Reservations are highly recommended during busy summer months.

activities.name: Skyline Trail Rugged Coastal Trek
activities.description: You will hike a beautiful wilderness loop trail that winds through spruce forests before opening onto a dramatic wooden boardwalk built over a sheer cliff face. Gaze down from the cliff edge to spot minke whales surfacing in the Gulf of St. Lawrence far below while eagle families soar overhead. Watching the sun set directly into the ocean from this high vantage point makes it one of Canada's most celebrated coastal hikes.
activities.location: Cabot Trail, Cape Breton Highlands National Park, NS
activities.duration_note: Requires a standard Parks Canada daily vehicle pass. The trail is fully open from June through October. Stay strictly on the designated wooden boardwalks to protect the fragile headland ecosystem.

activities.name: Traditional Celtic Kitchen Party at The Lower Deck
activities.description: You will step into a historic sandstone warehouse along the Halifax waterfront to join a legendary East Coast kitchen party. Grab a pint of local Alexander Keith's beer and sing along to high-energy, live maritime folk bands playing traditional fiddles, tin whistles, and acoustic guitars. The lively atmosphere and friendly crowd will have you stamping your feet along with locals all night long.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Live traditional music sets run nightly during the summer season and on weekends in winter. Alcohol sales in Nova Scotia are restricted to specialized NSLC stores.

activities.name: Green Gables Heritage Place Cultural Tour
activities.description: You will explore the green-roofed 19th-century farmhouse that inspired L.M. Montgomery’s classic novel, 'Anne of Green Gables.' Walk through rooms carefully restored to their 1890s style, then stroll along the quiet paths of the Haunted Wood and Lover’s Lane. It is a nostalgic step into literary history that brings the island's romantic farming heritage and coastal beauty vividly to life.
activities.duration_note: Full seasonal operations run from May through October. Limited access or total closure occurs during the winter months. Perfect family-friendly cultural experience with easy walking paths.

activities.name: Western Brook Pond Fjord Boat Tour
activities.description: You will complete a scenic 3-kilometer walk across flat peat bogs to board a custom boat and cruise deep into a spectacular landlocked fjord. Sail beneath monumental, sheer rock cliffs that tower 600 meters above waters carved by ancient glaciers thousands of years ago. Feeling the cool mountain breeze while viewing cascading waterfalls tumble down the vertical rock faces is an incredible wilderness experience.
activities.location: Western Brook Pond Trailhead, Highway 430, NL
activities.duration_note: Requires a 3km walk from the parking lot to reach the boat launch. Operates from June to mid-September. Requires a Parks Canada park entry pass in addition to your boat tour ticket.

activities.name: Signal Hill Citadel & Coastal Hike
activities.description: You will hike up the rugged paths of Signal Hill to stand outside Cabot Tower, where Guglielmo Marconi famously received the world’s first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901. Gaze down from the high cliffs to watch fishing boats navigate the narrow 'Narrows' harbor entrance while spotting seasonal icebergs floating offshore. The historic stone tower and surrounding military gun batteries offer a fascinating look into Canada's early global communications history.
activities.location: Signal Hill Rd, St. John's, NL
activities.duration_note: The historic grounds are open year-round, but visitor center operations run from May to October. The hillside paths are exposed to strong Atlantic winds; warm windproof layers are recommended.

activities.name: Aurora Borealis Viewing Experience at Aurora Village
activities.description: You will settle into a traditional, wood-heated teepee situated along the edge of a pristine, frozen subarctic lake away from city light pollution. Step outside into the crisp winter air to watch bright ribbons of green and violet northern lights dance across the dark night sky. Warming up by a crackling fire with a hot cup of maple tea while waiting for the lights to shimmer overhead is an unforgettable subarctic experience.
activities.duration_note: Strictly seasonal with operations divided between winter (December to April) and late summer (mid-August to September). Winter requires renting specialized high-grade thermal clothing.

activities.name: Tundra Buggy Polar Bear Expedition
activities.description: You will board a massive, custom-built Tundra Buggy equipped with enormous tires to travel safely across the barren landscapes of the subarctic plains. Explore the icy shores of Hudson Bay to view wild polar bears up close as they wait for the winter sea ice to freeze over. Watching these massive apex predators look up at your vehicle from just feet away offers a rare and powerful wildlife encounter.
activities.duration_note: The peak polar bear migration season runs strictly from October through November each year. Requires booking months in advance due to strict environmental limits on vehicle permits.

activities.name: Yukon River Wilderness Canoe Trip
activities.description: You will launch a classic expedition canoe into the swift currents of the historic Yukon River, paddling past forested valleys and old gold-rush ruins. Sleep at remote river camps under the late-night midnight sun, cooking meals over a campfire while watching for wild bald eagles and bears along the banks. It is a rewarding wilderness journey that lets you follow the historic paths of early northern explorers.
activities.duration_note: Available from June through September when the northern rivers are ice-free. Price includes a heavy-duty expedition canoe rental, safety barrels, life jackets, and regional river maps.

activities.name: The Infamous Sourtoe Cocktail Challenge
activities.description: You will belly up to the historic wooden bar inside the Downtown Hotel to take part in an eccentric, world-famous northern gold rush tradition. Order a shot of Yukon Jack whisky containing a real, dehydrated human toe that has been preserved in salt. To earn your official certificate, you must drink the shot while following the club's strict rule: 'You can drink it fast, you can drink it slow, but your lips must touch the toe.'
activities.location: Sourdough Saloon, 2nd Ave & Queen St, Dawson City, YT
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. The toe itself is not ingested; a steep $2,500 CAD fine is strictly enforced if a guest accidentally swallows it. Participants must be of legal provincial drinking age.

activities.name: Inuit Printmaking Workshop at the Kinngait Studios
activities.description: You will travel to a world-renowned Arctic art collective to work alongside talented Inuit stonecutters and printmakers. Learn traditional print techniques using local stone blocks to create your own unique piece of artwork depicting northern wildlife and community legends. It is a profound, creative window into how contemporary Inuit art preserves rich cultural histories across generations.
activities.location: Kinngait Studios, Cape Dorset (Fly-in from Iqaluit), NU
activities.duration_note: Open year-round by appointment. Reaching the remote island studio requires booking an regional Arctic flight; plan your travel budget carefully around flight schedules.

activities.name: Local Craft Beer Tasting at Woodcutter's Blanket
activities.description: You will step inside a beautifully restored, historic log cabin from the 1930s to relax at Whitehorse’s premier cocktail and craft beer lounge. Pull up a stool to sample locally brewed northern IPAs and creative cocktails mixed with foraged wild berries and spruce tips. The cozy wood interiors paired with a welcoming local crowd offer a perfect way to experience the Yukon's warm hospitality.
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. Note that alcohol in the Yukon is tightly regulated and sold through dedicated territorial liquor stores rather than standard corner convenience stores.

activities.name: Eclipse Nordic Hot Springs Soak
activities.description: You will submerge yourself in rich mineral waters at a modern wellness facility surrounded by snow-covered pine forests. Relax in the outdoor stone pools where natural, geothermal water flows at a soothing 40 degrees Celsius. If visiting during the freezing winter months, you can participate in the fun local 'Hair Freezing Contest,' shaping your frozen white hair into wild shapes in the subarctic air.
activities.location: KM 10 Takhini Hot Springs Rd, Whitehorse, YT
activities.duration_note: Open year-round. The modern facility is strictly adult-only (ages 19 and older). Advanced online booking is required to secure your timed entry slot on winter weekends.

activities.name: Midnight Dome Panoramic Overlook
activities.description: You will drive up a winding mountain road to reach a spectacular summit viewpoint towering high above the historic streets of Dawson City. Look out from the peak to see the beautiful Klondike and Yukon rivers meet against a backdrop of rolling northern mountains. If visiting during the height of summer, you can sit out at midnight to watch the sun dip close to the horizon without ever setting.
activities.location: Midnight Dome Rd, Dawson City, YT
activities.duration_note: Completely free public access. The road to the summit is gravel and only open to vehicles from mid-May through October; winter access requires snowmobiles or snowshoes.
